title: Group Internal Lines | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our hardware in CLO 2025.1 allows you to quickly group internal lines using shortcuts, with grouping preserved during pattern edits.

Check out other new features here:https://clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Okay, so here I have my 2D window, and I'm going to show you some fun updates we have with our internal lines. First thing is the improvement to grouping. So with my transform pattern tool selected, shortcut A, I can select my two internal lines holding down shift, and then right-clicking right on top of them, you could always get to group, and then you can group the internal lines. But now we have that shortcut where you can just select these two holding down shift and then hit Control-G. For Max, it'd be Command-G. Then once you're done grouping, you can select your internal lines. Once they're selected and grouped, you can see that now you can move them around, and they'll all be grouped together. They'll keep the grouping even if you decide to, like, cut this right here. So if I decide to cut this pattern, the grouping will still stay, as you can see. And even if I decide to re-merge this together, they're grouping will stay. The only way that it's not going to group is if you select it, right-click, and ungroup them. Pretty cool. Now, another really cool update we've done with the internal lines is with this center line. Now you can extend it to that center line. Going to your Edit Pattern tool, you can then select the internal line, right-click right on top of it, and then extend to Trim, and then you can say to Unfolded Line. And then it will extend to the Unfolded Line. And you can see that there's only one internal line, and it's great. It will not work with Add Point. Like, if I select this, right-click, Extend slash Trim to Add Point, it's not going to be there. That's because you cannot add a point. To that center line, right? Because you can only add segment points to pattern outlines, and the center line is not a pattern outline. So that's why that doesn't work. It makes sense. But you can, of course, go to Extend slash Trim, and then to Unfolded Line. We also added this if you decided to distribute. So if I went to my back pattern here and selected these two pattern outlines, right-clicked on top and said, Distribute Internal Line Between Segments, I then have an option right here, Extend to Unfolded Line. And then it will extend to this half. I can then increase, right? I can also say I want it to be a straight line, anything like that. And then I can hit OK. And then the other one will be created. markdown_content: # Group Internal Lines | CLO 2025.1 Features Deep Dive This document details the new features and improvements related to **internal lines grouping** and **extension options** in CLO 2025.1, focusing on pattern editing tools like the Transform Pattern tool, Edit Pattern tool, and new commands such as "Extend to Unfolded Line" and "Distribute Internal Line Between Segments." --- ## Grouping Internal Lines Improvements This section explains the enhanced workflow for grouping internal lines in CLO 2025.1, including new shortcuts and behavior that preserves grouping during pattern edits. - Select multiple internal lines using the Transform Pattern tool (shortcut **A**). - Hold **Shift** and select the desired lines. - Previously, grouping was accessible by right-clicking and selecting **Group**. - Now, a shortcut allows grouping by pressing **Ctrl+G** (Windows) or **Command+G** (Mac). - Once grouped, internal lines move as a single unit. - The grouping persists even if the pattern is cut or re-merged. - To break the grouping, you must explicitly select the group, right-click, and choose **Ungroup**. - This update improves workflow efficiency by maintaining group integrity through editing operations. --- ## Extending Internal Lines to the Center Line and Unfolded Line This section covers the new capability to extend internal lines to the center line or unfolded line within the Edit Pattern tool, alongside related limitations. - Using the **Edit Pattern tool**, select an internal line. - Right-click and choose **Extend/Trim > To Unfolded Line**. - This extends the internal line to the unfolded pattern edge or center line. - The feature works only with "Unfolded Line" extension and not with "Add Point". - **Add Point** is unavailable because points cannot be added to center lines, which are not pattern outlines. - This restriction aligns with CLO’s pattern editing logic, where segment points apply only to pattern outlines. - This extension feature streamlines internal line adjustments without needing manual edits. --- ## Distributing Internal Lines Between Segments with Extension This section describes the ability to distribute internal lines evenly between pattern segments, with options to extend lines to the unfolded edge. - Select two pattern outlines in the 2D window. - Right-click and choose **Distribute Internal Line Between Segments**. - An option is available to **Extend to Unfolded Line** for these internal lines. - You can specify parameters such as whether the line should be straight. - Upon confirmation, CLO generates the internal lines extended to the unfolded edge. - This update facilitates precise and automated internal line placement, improving pattern accuracy and saving time. --- # Summary CLO 2025.1 introduces key enhancements to internal line management, including shortcut grouping of internal lines with persistent groupings through edits, new commands to extend internal lines to center or unfolded lines, and distributing internal lines between segments with extension options. These features improve pattern editing workflows, maintain structural integrity, and offer greater control over internal line placement.
